#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Daily release-draft sweeper (issue #282), rides daily-publish.yml:
#
#   - lists DRAFT releases older than $SWEEP_MAX_AGE_SECONDS (default 24h);
#   - deletes stale drafts created by the pipeline (author.type == Bot, a
#     *[bot] login, the repo's machine account (DAILY_PUBLISH_ASSIGNEE,
#     default ai-teammate — gh-2287: its drafts (ai-gh-*/ai-pr-*) are
#     User-typed and marker-less but machine-created), OR the body
#     carries a well-formed `release-draft-owner: run/<id>/job/<job>`
#     marker — the exact shape
#     release_lazy_draft.sh / release_attach_or_create.sh stamp and
#     release_draft_guard.sh parses; since the drafts are created with
#     GH_TOKEN=RELEASE_PAT the API author is the PAT's human owner, so
#     the marker is the only ownership proof, gh-2008. Prose that merely
#     MENTIONS the substring or a malformed marker is NOT ownership —
#     those drafts stay human/kept, E1) — draft assets are unpublished by
#     definition and published releases are the artifact store, so
#     deletion is safe (issue #282 E2). The git tag is never touched;
#   - stale HUMAN drafts are listed in the summary, never deleted (E1);
#   - fresh drafts (<24h) are counted, never touched — an in-flight run
#     may legitimately own them. EXCEPTION (gh-2318): a fresh draft with a
#     well-formed release-draft-owner marker is RECLAIMED immediately when
#     its owner run completed, no ci.yml push train on the tag is still
#     queued/in-flight, and the tag's newest concluded ci.yml push train
#     failed with release-provenance SKIPPED (the publish point is
#     unreachable — rerun --failed cannot resurrect skipped jobs, so
#     nobody will ever publish it; the same criterion as ci.yml's gh-2230
#     train-draft-guard, which only sees drafts visible at train end).
#     A rerunnable (FAILED) provenance keeps the draft as the rerun
#     --failed recovery vessel (gh-1899) until it goes stale below;
#   - files ONE deduplicated, self-closing issue (label release-hygiene)
#     whenever anything stale was found — a comment on the open issue
#     instead of a duplicate, auto-closed again once a sweep comes up
#     clean (same convention as nightly.yml / daily_publish_report.sh).
#
# ── orphaned twin drafts are lifecycle-managed hygiene (gh-2372) ───────────
# A MARKED pipeline draft whose tag ALREADY carries a PUBLISHED release is
# a proven orphan twin of the same-run sibling view→create race (v1.0.760:
# the build-extension draft won + was published, the build-macos-cli twin
# rotted 43h and was swept with the misleading "a `gh release create` step
# died" prose; v1.0.763's twin rotted while counted "fresh"). No run can
# ever publish or attach into such a draft — uploads resolve the published
# object by tag — and release_draft_twin_dedupe.sh now self-deletes the
# loser at create time, so any twin the sweep still sees is a best-effort
# leftover. The sweep reclaims these drafts IMMEDIATELY (fresh or stale)
# as routine hygiene (gh-236 convention: visible in the summary, never a
# stale-draft finding — a residual twin must not re-file the recurring
# issue), and the clean-sweep auto-close names the reclaims. Ownership
# proof stays required: an UNMARKED author-bot draft on a published tag
# keeps the bot-bucket finding (no marker → no ownership → existing
# behavior).
#
# ── artefact-cache drafts have their own lifecycle (gh-236) ────────────────
# The machine loop (dmtools-agents factory: timerAutoCommitAndSave.js →
# releaseArtefacts.uploadRawFile → github_get_or_create_draft_release, tag
# template `ai-{ticketKey}`) writes every fa leg's session/output snapshots
# as assets of a per-ticket DRAFT release `ai-gh-<n>` / `ai-pr-<n>`, created
# with the ai-teammate token — User-typed, marker-less, no Actions run owns
# it. Those drafts are caches by design (never published, assets
# best-effort), NOT failed release-train drafts — but without a lifecycle
# they rotted 24h, were swept as generic bot-bucket findings, and re-filed
# the recurring sweep issue every day (gh-2287 → gh-2318 → gh-236). The
# guard: a machine-account draft whose tag matches `ai-(gh|pr)-<digits>` is
#   - RECLAIMED NOW, any age, when the ticket entity is `closed` — a closed
#     cycle never resumes (a reopened ticket starts a fresh session; the
#     pack's restore path is non-fatal and recreates the cache on "first
#     run"), so the draft is provably garbage the moment the cycle ends;
#   - swept by the existing 24h backstop when the ticket is still open (a
#     parked leg — the cache is recreated if the leg resumes);
#   - kept untouched while the ticket is open and the draft is fresh (an
#     in-flight leg may be writing snapshots into it);
#   - KEPT on any ticket-state lookup failure (never delete blind) — only
#     the 24h backstop then applies.
# The class is EXCLUDED from the sweep-issue finding counters: reclaiming a
# lifecycle-managed cache is routine hygiene, not a stale-draft finding, so
# the issue auto-closes when only cache traffic remains. Human-authored
# `ai-*` drafts are NOT lifecycle-managed (E1 holds — they stay listed,
# kept), and machine-authored non-matching drafts (e.g. a machine-authored
# `vX.Y.Z` train draft) stay in the bot bucket and remain findings.
#
# Drafts are deleted by release id via the API: a draft may carry an empty
# tag_name, which makes every tag-based `gh release delete` ambiguous.
#
# Env: GITHUB_REPOSITORY, GH_TOKEN, SWEEP_MAX_AGE_SECONDS (default 86400),
#      SWEEP_LABEL (default release-hygiene).
set -euo pipefail

repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:?GITHUB_REPOSITORY must be set}"
max_age="${SWEEP_MAX_AGE_SECONDS:-86400}"
label="${SWEEP_LABEL:-release-hygiene}"
# The repo's machine-account identity (same env + default as
# daily_publish_report.sh): drafts authored by it are pipeline-created —
# gh-2287: the ai-teammate factory's drafts (ai-gh-*/ai-pr-*) are User-typed
# and marker-less, so author-only Bot detection bucketed them as human and
# they rotted forever while the sweep issue never auto-closed.
assignee="${DAILY_PUBLISH_ASSIGNEE:-ai-teammate}"
title="[daily-publish] stale release drafts swept"
daily_url="${GITHUB_SERVER_URL:-https://github.com}/$repo/actions/runs/${GITHUB_RUN_ID:-manual}"

# ── failed-train diagnosis (gh-2105 + gh-2318) ──────────────────────────────
# The staged draft's publish owner is the TAG TRAIN (ci.yml's push run on
# the tag ref — release-provenance is the sole publish point, gh-1801).
# Diagnose <tag>'s newest CONCLUDED failed ci.yml push train; prints one
# TSV row:
#
#   train_id <TAB> conclusion <TAB> url <TAB> failed_jobs <TAB> prov_conclusion <TAB> in_flight
#
# `failed_jobs` names the train's failure-concluded jobs (the gh-2105 issue
# prose). `prov_conclusion` is the release-provenance job's OWN conclusion —
# "skipped" means the publish point is UNREACHABLE (`rerun --failed` never
# resurrects skipped jobs — the gh-2230 train-guard criterion), "failure"
# means it is rerunnable (the staged draft is the `rerun --failed` recovery
# vessel, gh-1899 — the stale 24h sweep reclaims it if the train is never
# recovered). `in_flight` is "in_flight" when ANY fetched ci.yml push run
# on the tag has a null conclusion (queued or in progress), "none" when all
# have concluded, and "unknown" if that check fails; the fresh-draft reclaim
# keeps unless it is explicitly "none", because a live train may still
# publish even when an older train failed. The publish-point job is matched
# by its ci.yml `name:` —
# "Sign release checksums" (pinned by test/release_stale_draft_reclaim_test.dart,
# gh-2318 group; update both together). Empty output = no failed train /
# lookup failed; every consumer degrades fail-safe (keep), and nothing
# here may gate the stale >24h delete (the diagnosis is never a
# precondition — gh-2105).
train_diagnosis() {
  local tag="$1" train_json failed_train train_id jobs_json in_flight
  train_json=$(gh run list --repo "$repo" --workflow ci.yml \
    --branch "$tag" --event push --limit 5 \
    --json databaseId,conclusion,url 2>/dev/null || echo "[]")
  in_flight=$(printf '%s' "$train_json" | jq -r '
    if any(.[]; .conclusion == null) then "in_flight" else "none" end
  ' 2>/dev/null || echo "unknown")
  failed_train=$(printf '%s' "$train_json" | jq -cr '
    ([.[] | select(.conclusion != "success" and .conclusion != null)][0]
      | if . == null then empty else
          {c: .conclusion, u: (.url // ""), i: .databaseId}
        end)' 2>/dev/null || echo "")
  [ -n "$failed_train" ] || return 0
  train_id=$(printf '%s' "$failed_train" | jq -r '.i // ""' 2>/dev/null || echo "")
  jobs_json=$(gh run view "$train_id" --repo "$repo" --json jobs 2>/dev/null || echo "")
  printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s' \
    "$train_id" \
    "$(printf '%s' "$failed_train" | jq -r '.c // "unknown"' 2>/dev/null || echo "unknown")" \
    "$(printf '%s' "$failed_train" | jq -r '.u // ""' 2>/dev/null || echo "")" \
    "$(printf '%s' "$jobs_json" | jq -r '[.jobs[] | select(.conclusion == "failure") | .name] | join(", ")' 2>/dev/null || echo "")" \
    "$(printf '%s' "$jobs_json" | jq -r '([.jobs[] | select(.name == "Sign release checksums")][0].conclusion // "")' 2>/dev/null || echo "")" \
    "$in_flight"
}


gh label create "$label" --repo "$repo" --color B60205 \
  --description "Auto-filed by the release-draft sweeper" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

# ── inventory ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# gh api --paginate emits one JSON array per page; the jq stream filter
# flattens them all. The roster is fetched ONCE and read twice: the draft
# rows below, plus (gh-2372) the set of tags that already carry a PUBLISHED
# release — the twin-orphan criterion. Bucketing happens in jq so the whole
# rule is reviewable in one place:
#   artifacts (machine account + ai-(gh|pr)-<n> tag — gh-236)
#                    -> lifecycle-managed: reclaim at cycle end / 24h
#                    backstop / keep in flight; NEVER a sweep finding
#   stale + pipeline (bot author, the machine account, or well-formed
#                    release-draft-owner: run/<id>/job/<job>
#                    marker in the body) -> delete, name the marker run
#   stale + human (no marker)          -> keep, list
#   fresh                              -> untouched, EXCEPT the gh-2318
#                    reclaim: a marked draft whose owner run completed and
#                    whose tag's train failed with release-provenance
#                    SKIPPED (publish point unreachable) is deleted NOW
roster=$(gh api --paginate "repos/$repo/releases")
# gh-2372: the tags that already carry a PUBLISHED release. Multi-page
# safe: the filter runs per page-array, so the joins are re-joined in bash.
published_tags=$(printf '%s' "$roster" \
  | jq -r '[.[] | select(.draft == false) | (.tag_name // "")] | join(" ")' \
  | tr '\n' ' ')
drafts=$(printf '%s' "$roster" | jq -r --argjson maxage "$max_age" --arg assignee "$assignee" '
  [ .[] | select(.draft == true)
    | { stale: ((now - (.created_at | fromdateiso8601)) > $maxage),
        bucket: (
          # gh-236 first: the machine loop artefact-cache class, keyed on
          # the machine account AND the `ai-{ticketKey}` tag shape the
          # factory releaseArtefacts.buildTag() produces (lowercased,
          # non-alnum to '-', so `GH-2288` becomes `ai-gh-2288`,
          # `pr-2293` becomes `ai-pr-2293`). Human-authored ai-* drafts and
          # machine-authored vX.Y.Z drafts never match and fall through to
          # the buckets below.
          if (((.author.login // "") == $assignee)
              and ((.tag_name // "") | test("^ai-(gh|pr)-[0-9]+$")))
          then "artifacts"
          elif ((now - (.created_at | fromdateiso8601)) > $maxage)
          then (if ((.author.type // "User") == "Bot"
                    or ((.author.login // "") | test("\\[bot\\]$"))
                    or ((.author.login // "") == $assignee)
                    or ((.body // "") | test("release-draft-owner: run/[0-9]+/job/")))
               then "bot" else "human" end)
          else "fresh" end),
        tag: (.tag_name // "(untagged)"),
        id: (.id | tostring),
        created: (.created_at // "?"),
        author: (.author.login // "unknown"),
        # Exact creating run parsed from the ownership marker ("" for
        # non-marker drafts) — the creating run executed on main, so a
        # tag-ref run lookup cannot find it (gh-2008). The capture
        # requires the WELL-FORMED run/<id>/job/<name> shape — the same
        # class the bucket rule above, release_draft_guard.sh and
        # release_draft_twin_dedupe.sh match: a body that merely MENTIONS
        # `release-draft-owner: run/<digits>/` without the /job/ segment
        # is prose, not ownership (E1) — its run stays "" so the twin
        # pre-check and the early-reclaim gates never act on it. The
        # array wrapper keeps exactly one value: a bare capture(...)? on a
        # non-matching body yields an EMPTY stream, and an empty field
        # would drop the whole draft row from the object stream.
        run: ([ (.body // "")
                | capture("release-draft-owner: run/(?<run>[0-9]+)/job/")?
                | .run ]
              | .[0] // "") } ]
  | sort_by(.created)[]
  # Column order matters: `read` collapses runs of whitespace IFS chars, so
  # the only possibly-EMPTY field (.run — marker-less drafts) must stay
  # LAST; .stale sits before it (gh-236: the artifacts branch branches on it).
  | [ .bucket, .tag, .id, .created, .author, .stale, .run ] | @tsv')

deleted=""
deleted_tags=""
deleted_count=0
failed_trains=0
# gh-2318: fresh (<24h) pipeline drafts reclaimed early — provably
# never-publishable (completed owner, failed train with skipped
# release-provenance). Tracked separately from the >24h sweep deletions.
reclaimed=""
reclaimed_tags=""
reclaimed_count=0
humans=""
human_tags=""
fresh_count=0
# gh-236: machine-loop artefact-cache drafts — lifecycle-managed, NOT
# sweep findings (reclaiming a cache whose ticket cycle ended is routine
# hygiene; the issue must auto-close when only cache traffic remains).
#   reclaimed at cycle end (ticket closed, any age) / swept by the 24h
#   backstop (ticket still open / state unknown) / kept (fresh + open).
art_reclaimed=""
art_reclaimed_tags=""
art_reclaimed_count=0
art_swept=""
art_swept_tags=""
art_swept_count=0
art_kept_tags=""
art_kept_count=0
# gh-2372: orphaned twin drafts (marked draft, tag already published) —
# lifecycle-managed hygiene like the artefact caches above: reclaimed at
# ANY age, visible in the summary, never a stale-draft finding.
twins=""
twin_tags=""
twin_count=0

while IFS=$'\t' read -r bucket tag id created author stale marker_run; do
  [ -n "$bucket" ] || continue
  # ── gh-2372 twin pre-check (before the bucket dispatch) ────────────────
  # A MARKED draft whose tag already carries a PUBLISHED release is a
  # proven orphan twin of the sibling create race: nothing can ever
  # publish or attach into it (uploads resolve the published object by
  # tag), and release_draft_twin_dedupe.sh now self-deletes the loser at
  # create time — anything the sweep still sees is a best-effort
  # leftover. Reclaimed at ANY age as routine hygiene, never a finding.
  # The artifacts bucket is excluded (lifecycle-managed above); unmarked
  # drafts have no ownership proof and stay in their buckets (E1).
  twin_published=false
  case " $published_tags " in *" $tag "*) twin_published=true ;; esac
  if [ "$twin_published" = "true" ] && [ -n "$marker_run" ] \
    && [ "$bucket" != "artifacts" ] && [ "$tag" != "(untagged)" ]; then
    gh api -X DELETE "repos/$repo/releases/$id" >/dev/null
    twin_count=$((twin_count + 1))
    twin_tags="$twin_tags $tag"
    run_url="${GITHUB_SERVER_URL:-https://github.com}/$repo/actions/runs/$marker_run"
    twins="$twins- \`$tag\` — created $created by @$author; creating run: $run_url\n  - reclaimed as an orphaned twin draft: the tag already carries a PUBLISHED release, so no run could ever publish or attach into this one (the same-run sibling create race won — gh-2372; self-deduped at create by release_draft_twin_dedupe.sh, this sweep is the backstop). Routine hygiene (gh-236 convention) — not a stale-draft finding.\n"
    continue
  fi
  case "$bucket" in
    artifacts)
      # gh-236: the machine loop's per-ticket artefact-cache draft
      # (`ai-gh-<n>` / `ai-pr-<n>` — timerAutoCommitAndSave.js snapshot
      # storage). The tag shape was validated by the jq bucket rule, so
      # `gh #<num>` / `pr #<num>` parsing below is total. State lookup:
      # the issues REST API serves PRs too (state=closed covers merged).
      # Any lookup failure yields an empty state — fail-safe: no early
      # reclaim, only the 24h backstop below may delete.
      rest="${tag#ai-}"
      kind="${rest%%-*}"
      num="${rest##*-}"
      state=$(gh api "repos/$repo/issues/$num" 2>/dev/null \
        | jq -r '.state // ""' 2>/dev/null || echo "")
      if [ "$state" = "closed" ]; then
        gh api -X DELETE "repos/$repo/releases/$id" >/dev/null
        art_reclaimed_count=$((art_reclaimed_count + 1))
        art_reclaimed="$art_reclaimed- \`$tag\` — created $created by @$author; ticket cycle ended (\`$kind #$num\` closed) — reclaimed at cycle end, no 24h wait: a closed cycle never resumes and the cache is recreated on any future first run (gh-236)\n"
        art_reclaimed_tags="$art_reclaimed_tags $tag"
      elif [ "$stale" = "true" ]; then
        gh api -X DELETE "repos/$repo/releases/$id" >/dev/null
        art_swept_count=$((art_swept_count + 1))
        art_swept="$art_swept- \`$tag\` — created $created by @$author; swept after 24h with the ticket still open or its state unknown (parked leg — the cache is recreated if the leg resumes; gh-236)\n"
        art_swept_tags="$art_swept_tags $tag"
      else
        art_kept_count=$((art_kept_count + 1))
        art_kept_tags="$art_kept_tags $tag"
      fi
      ;;
    fresh)
      # gh-2318: "fresh — untouched" is right while an in-flight run may
      # own the draft, but a fresh draft can already be PROVABLY
      # never-publishable: the v1.0.739 shape — a daily-child staging leg
      # minted the tag (release_tag_mint.sh) and staged the draft, the
      # freshly fired train failed upstream of release-provenance, and the
      # gh-2230 train-draft-guard either ran before the draft existed (a
      # long attach leg created it later) or kept it while its owner was
      # still in-flight. Nothing re-examined such a draft with train
      # knowledge, so it rotted the full 24h and re-filed the recurring
      # sweep issue. Apply the train guard's EXACT criterion here —
      # reclaim only a well-formed-marker draft whose owner run COMPLETED,
      # whose tag has NO queued/in-flight ci.yml push train, and whose
      # newest concluded ci.yml push train failed with release-provenance
      # SKIPPED (rerun --failed cannot resurrect skipped jobs — nobody
      # will ever publish it). Fail-safe keeps mirror the train guard:
      # unmarked/human drafts (E1), an in-flight owner run (possibly
      # mid-upload), ANY queued/in-flight tag train (it may still publish
      # even when an older train failed), a rerunnable FAILED provenance
      # (that draft stays the `rerun --failed` recovery vessel, gh-1899,
      # until the stale sweep), any lookup failure (never delete blind),
      # and untagged drafts (no train to diagnose).
      if [ -n "$marker_run" ] && [ "$tag" != "(untagged)" ]; then
        owner_status=$(gh run view "$marker_run" --repo "$repo" --json status 2>/dev/null \
          | jq -r '.status // empty' 2>/dev/null || echo "")
        if [ "$owner_status" = "completed" ]; then
          diag=$(train_diagnosis "$tag")
          train_url_found=$(printf '%s' "$diag" | cut -f3)
          failed_jobs=$(printf '%s' "$diag" | cut -f4)
          prov_conclusion=$(printf '%s' "$diag" | cut -f5)
          train_conclusion=$(printf '%s' "$diag" | cut -f2)
          train_in_flight=$(printf '%s' "$diag" | cut -f6)
          if [ -n "$diag" ] && [ "$prov_conclusion" = "skipped" ] \
            && [ "$train_in_flight" = "none" ]; then
            gh api -X DELETE "repos/$repo/releases/$id" >/dev/null
            reclaimed_count=$((reclaimed_count + 1))
            failed_trains=$((failed_trains + 1))
            run_url="${GITHUB_SERVER_URL:-https://github.com}/$repo/actions/runs/$marker_run"
            train_line="  - tag train: ${train_url_found:-<url unavailable>} concluded ${train_conclusion:-unknown} — the staged draft was never published (release-provenance, the sole publish point, is gated behind the tag train; a superseded failed train is never rerun — verify_pubdev_release.sh heals the LATEST tag only)"
            [ -n "$failed_jobs" ] && train_line="$train_line; failed jobs: $failed_jobs"
            reclaimed="$reclaimed- \`$tag\` — created $created by @$author; creating run: $run_url\n  - reclaimed early: the draft is younger than $((max_age / 3600))h but its publish point is unreachable (failed train, skipped release-provenance — rerun --failed cannot resurrect skipped jobs), so no in-flight run can own it and nobody will ever publish it (gh-2318)\n$train_line\n"
            reclaimed_tags="$reclaimed_tags $tag"
            continue
          fi
        fi
      fi
      fresh_count=$((fresh_count + 1))
      ;;
    human)
      humans="$humans- \`$tag\` — created $created by @$author (human draft: listed, kept)\n"
      human_tags="$human_tags $tag"
      ;;
    bot)
      gh api -X DELETE "repos/$repo/releases/$id" >/dev/null
      deleted_count=$((deleted_count + 1))
      # Name the creating run so a RECURRING stuck draft points at its
      # broken step instead of rotting silently (AC2). Marker drafts name
      # it exactly (the stamping scripts write run/<id>); untagged
      # author-bot drafts fall back to the newest run on the tag ref;
      # dispatch-time drafts have no run on their ref — then say so.
      run_url=""
      if [ -n "$marker_run" ]; then
        run_url="${GITHUB_SERVER_URL:-https://github.com}/$repo/actions/runs/$marker_run"
      elif [ "$tag" != "(untagged)" ]; then
        run_url=$(gh run list --repo "$repo" --branch "$tag" --limit 1 \
          --json url --jq '.[0].url // empty' 2>/dev/null || true)
      fi
      if [ -z "$run_url" ]; then
        if [ "$author" = "$assignee" ]; then
          # gh-2287: a machine-account draft carries no marker (the
          # automation created it with its own token, outside this repo's
          # runners) — name the account as the creator; the dispatch-time
          # "creating step died mid-run" prose below would misdirect the
          # RCA (gh-2105 class) — nothing died.
          run_url="the @$assignee automation loop (machine-account draft — created outside this repo's runners, no Actions run owns it)"
        else
          run_url="no run on ref \`$tag\` (dispatch-time draft — the creating step died mid-run)"
        fi
      fi
      # gh-2105: the staging draft's publish owner is the TAG TRAIN
      # (ci.yml's push run on the tag ref — release-provenance is the
      # sole publish point, gh-1801). When that train failed, the
      # creating run named above is NOT the broken step — the train is,
      # and a superseded failed train is never rerun
      # (verify_pubdev_release.sh heals the LATEST tag only). Name it
      # (URL + conclusion + failed jobs) so the sweep issue points at
      # the true blocker. Any lookup failure degrades to the static
      # prose below — the delete + issue filing must never depend on
      # the diagnosis.
      train_line=""
      if [ "$tag" != "(untagged)" ]; then
        diag=$(train_diagnosis "$tag")
        if [ -n "$diag" ]; then
          train_conclusion=$(printf '%s' "$diag" | cut -f2)
          train_url_found=$(printf '%s' "$diag" | cut -f3)
          failed_jobs=$(printf '%s' "$diag" | cut -f4)
          failed_trains=$((failed_trains + 1))
          train_line="  - tag train: ${train_url_found:-<url unavailable>} concluded ${train_conclusion:-unknown} — the staged draft was never published (release-provenance, the sole publish point, is gated behind the tag train; a superseded failed train is never rerun — verify_pubdev_release.sh heals the LATEST tag only)"
          [ -n "$failed_jobs" ] && train_line="$train_line; failed jobs: $failed_jobs"
          train_line="$train_line\n"
        fi
      fi
      deleted="$deleted- \`$tag\` — created $created by @$author; creating run: $run_url\n$train_line"
      deleted_tags="$deleted_tags $tag"
      ;;
  esac
done <<< "$drafts"

# ── issue lifecycle (dedup + self-closing) ─────────────────────────────────
find_open_issue() { # echoes the issue number of the open sweep issue, or nothing
  gh issue list --repo "$repo" --state open --label "$label" \
    --limit 100 --json number,title --jq '.[] | [.number, .title] | @tsv' 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS=$'\t' read -r n t; do
        if [ "$t" = "$title" ]; then echo "$n"; fi
      done | head -1
}

same_run_issues() { # gh-2359 AC3: open issues already filed from THIS run
  # The run URL is the join key (the leg-filer embeds the same
  # **Daily run:**/**Sweep run:** URL): a sweep finding and a leg failure
  # from one daily run (the #2336/#2337 shape) share roots even though
  # their error signatures never match.
  # gh itself has no --arg flag — the filter runs through real jq, exactly
  # like this script's `gh api --paginate … | jq -r --arg …` draft lookups.
  gh issue list --repo "$repo" --state open --limit 200 --json number,body \
    2>/dev/null \
    | jq -r --arg run_url "$daily_url" \
      '.[] | select((.body // "") | contains($run_url)) | .number' \
    || true
}

stale_count=$((deleted_count + reclaimed_count + $(printf '%s' "$humans" | grep -c . || true) ))

if [ "$stale_count" -gt 0 ]; then
  body=$(mktemp)
  {
    echo "**Sweep run:** $daily_url"
    echo "**Swept:** $deleted_count stale pipeline-created draft(s) older than $((max_age / 3600))h"
    printf '%b' "$deleted"
    # gh-2318: fresh drafts reclaimed early — their publish point is
    # unreachable, so the 24h wait would only delay the inevitable and
    # keep the sweep issue recurring (see the branch comment for the
    # full fail-safe keep list).
    if [ "$reclaimed_count" -gt 0 ]; then
      echo
      echo "**Reclaimed early (<$((max_age / 3600))h):** $reclaimed_count fresh pipeline draft(s) whose publish point is unreachable (gh-2318)"
      printf '%b' "$reclaimed"
    fi
    [ -n "$humans" ] && { echo; echo "**Kept (human drafts, listed not deleted — E1):**"; printf '%b' "$humans"; }
    # gh-236: cache lifecycle activity rides the filed issue for
    # visibility — in its own section, with the release-failure prose
    # never attached (nothing died, nothing failed to publish). It does
    # NOT contribute to the finding count above.
    if [ "$((art_reclaimed_count + art_swept_count))" -gt 0 ]; then
      echo
      echo "**Artefact-cache drafts (machine-loop \`ai-gh-*\`/\`ai-pr-*\` caches — lifecycle-managed, not release failures):** $art_reclaimed_count reclaimed at cycle end, $art_swept_count swept after 24h"
      printf '%b' "$art_reclaimed"
      printf '%b' "$art_swept"
    fi
    # gh-2372: orphaned twin reclaims ride the filed issue for visibility —
    # own section, hygiene prose, never part of the finding counters.
    if [ "$twin_count" -gt 0 ]; then
      echo
      echo "**Orphaned twin drafts (gh-2372 — lifecycle-managed hygiene, not release failures):** $twin_count reclaimed"
      printf '%b' "$twins"
    fi
    echo
    echo "**Fresh drafts (<$((max_age / 3600))h):** $fresh_count — untouched (an in-flight run may own them)"
    if [ "$art_kept_count" -gt 0 ]; then
      echo "**Artefact-cache drafts kept (ticket in flight):** $art_kept_count — reclaimed when the cycle closes, swept after 24h if parked (gh-236)"
    fi
    echo
    if [ "$failed_trains" -gt 0 ]; then
      echo "**Failed tag trains named above:** $failed_trains"
      echo
      echo "A stale draft whose tag train failed means the publish owner never ran — the draft was the gh-1801 staging draft and release-provenance (its sole publish point) is gated behind the failed train. Rerun the train if the tag should still ship; recurrence means a lifecycle guard is missing (issue #282)."
    elif [ "$deleted_count" -gt 0 ]; then
      echo "A stale draft means a \`gh release create\` step died between asset upload and publish — check the creating run's failed step. Recurrence means a lifecycle guard is missing (issue #282)."
    else
      # Findings are kept human drafts only (gh-236: cache lifecycle
      # traffic is excluded from the finding counters) — the create-death
      # prose would misdirect: nothing died and nothing failed to publish.
      echo "Kept human drafts above are listed, never deleted (E1) — delete by hand once done with them. Machine-loop artefact-cache drafts (\`ai-gh-*\`/\`ai-pr-*\`) are lifecycle-managed (gh-236): reclaimed when their ticket cycle closes, swept after 24h when the ticket stays open or its state is unknown."
    fi
    echo
    echo "---"
    echo "Auto-filed by the daily draft sweeper; auto-closes when a sweep finds nothing stale."
  } > "$body"
  existing=$(find_open_issue)
  # gh-2359 AC3: peers computed BEFORE the create (eventual consistency).
  peers=$(same_run_issues)
  if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
    gh issue comment "$existing" --repo "$repo" --body-file "$body" >/dev/null
    issue_action="commented on #$existing (still finding stale drafts)"
  else
    created_issue=$(gh issue create --repo "$repo" --title "$title" \
      --body-file "$body" --label bug --label "$label" --assignee "$assignee" 2>/dev/null || true)
    issue_action="filed ${created_issue:-<issue creation failed>}"
    if [ -n "$created_issue" ] && [ -n "$peers" ]; then
      # gh-2359 AC3: the sweep finding is filed from the same run as
      # another open issue (typically a leg failure) — cross-link so the
      # shared root is visible before anyone fixes each in parallel.
      peer_list=$(printf '%s' "$peers" | awk '{printf "%s#%s", (NR > 1 ? ", " : ""), $1}')
      gh issue comment "${created_issue##*/}" --repo "$repo" \
        --body "**Same-run cross-link (gh-2359):** same run as ${peer_list} — roots may be shared. One failing run can surface as several findings; check whether a single root cause covers them before fixing each in parallel." >/dev/null
      issue_action+=" + cross-linked with same-run issue(s) ${peer_list}"
    fi
  fi

  issue_action="none needed"
  if [ -n "$existing" ]; then

    issue_action="auto-closed #$existing (clean sweep)"
  fi
fi

Found the smoking gun for the ubuntu-latest job:

``
release_notes_cap: /tmp/release-lazy-notes.67hgBr bounded 11961 bytes (was 139735, cap 120000)
HTTP 500 (https://api.github.com/repos/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/releases)
##[error]the draft create for v1.0.78 failed (rc 1) and no concurrent release appeared — nothing to attach to; fix the create failure above (e.g. the release body exceeding the 125,000-character API cap, gh-237)
``

So the draft creation failed with HTTP 500. Interesting — "HTTP 500" from `POST /releases`. The release_notes_cap bounded the notes to 11961 bytes (under 120000). But then `gh release create` got an HTTP 500.

Wait — HTTP 500 from GitHub API on release create... That's a server error, but the message mentions gh-237: "the release body exceeding the 125,000-character API cap".

Hmm, the note was capped at 11961 BYTES. But the API cap is 125,000 CHARACTERS? If the body has multi-byte UTF-8 characters, 119,961 bytes could be < 125,000 chars... no wait, bytes >= chars for multi-byte. 11961 bytes ≤ 125000 chars would be satisfied since bytes > chars means chars < bytes. Hmm, chars ≤ bytes, so 11961 bytes → chars ≤ 11961 < 125000. So the character cap is fine.

But wait — HTTP 500 is a server error. Possibly caused by an oversized body? GitHub returns 422 for oversized. A 500 could be transient... but all three failed jobs (ubuntu-latest x64, ubuntu-24.04-arm arm64, windows-latest zip) failed the same way? Let me check the windows and arm logs.

Actually the release_lazy_draft.sh script runs in each matrix job; the first job to create the draft wins, others attach. Actually — the draft `v1.0.78` WAS created (created 2026-11-25T15:15:39Z... wait, that's before this run even started? The run createdAt is 2026-11-25T15:15:43Z. Hmm, draft created_at 15:15:39Z — 4 seconds BEFORE run creation? Odd. Actually created_at on a draft release is when the draft object was created... The run was created at 15:15:43. The draft at 15:15:39. Weird, but the daily-child leg minted the tag & staged the draft? Actually per gh-2318 comment in the sweep script: "a daily-child staging leg minted the tag (release_tag_mint.sh) and staged the draft, the freshly fired train failed upstream of release-provenance". So the draft was staged by the daily child at 15:15:39, and the train started at 15:15:43.

OK so the draft already existed when the matrix jobs ran. Then why did `release_lazy_draft.sh` try to CREATE and get HTTP 500? Let me read release_lazy_draft.sh to understand. Presumably: if the draft exists, attach to it; if not, create. The HTTP 500 came from a create attempt... but the draft existed already? Hmm, maybe the concurrent-create race handling: it tried create, got 500, then checked "no concurrent release appeared". 

Wait — actually the sweep says the draft WAS created (v1.0.78, created by @github-actions[bot], creating run 45643151796). So SOME job's create succeeded eventually. Which job created it? The macOS self-hosted jobs succeeded (16:00-16:10). So maybe one of the macOS jobs created the draft successfully at ~16:10... but draft created_at says 15:15:39Z. Hmm.

Let me look at release_lazy_draft.sh to understand the create/attach flow, and check the other two failed jobs' logs.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Lazy DRAFT create for the release train's asset-upload steps (gh-1801).
#
# The train workflows (ci.yml binaries/web-spa, build-macos.yml
# build-macos-cli/build-extension) need a release object to attach assets
# to, but the release must never go live from an upload step: `fa update`
# resolves the `latest` release and hard-fails without the SIGNED
# SHA256SUMS(.sig) (bin/self_manage.dart provenance gate), which only the
# tag-run release-provenance job can upload. This script creates the
# release as a DRAFT — nothing else:
#
#   - body = scripts/release_notes.sh output (curated `## <version>`
#     CHANGELOG section → curated `## Unreleased` → conventional commits;
#     the gh-1172 curated-notes contract), with a minimal fallback —
#     never `--generate-notes` (review threads 3/7);
#   - body carries `<!-- release-draft-owner: run/<run_id>/job/<job> -->`
#     so scripts/release_draft_guard.sh can reclaim the draft on failure
#     (review threads 4/8) — matrix legs override the identity via
#     RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY (e.g. binaries-linux-x64) so a failed leg's
#     guard can never match a sibling's in-flight draft;
#   - the view→create race is tolerated (`|| true`): a sibling leg or the
#     attach path may create the release between our view and create —
#     the loser just uploads into the winner's release;
#   - it NEVER publishes and NEVER flags latest: the single publish point
#     of a tag train is release-provenance's "Upload provenance assets"
#     step (`gh release edit --draft=false --latest` after SHA256SUMS.sig
#     lands). A red provenance leaves the previous release as latest —
#     safe degradation, never a provenance-less latest (v1.0.630 window).
#
# Usage: release_lazy_draft.sh <tag>
# Env: GITHUB_REPOSITORY, GITHUB_RUN_ID, GITHUB_JOB (Actions defaults),
#      RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY (optional leg-suffixed override),
#      GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN.
set -euo pipefail

tag="${1:?usage: release_lazy_draft.sh <tag>}"
repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:?GITHUB_REPOSITORY must be set}"
identity="${RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY:-run/${GITHUB_RUN_ID:?GITHUB_RUN_ID must be set (GitHub Actions default env)}/job/${GITHUB_JOB:?GITHUB_JOB must be set (GitHub Actions default env)}}"

# The guard greps exactly this class — validate here so a malformed
# override fails loud instead of stamping a marker the guard could never
# match (a forever-orphaned draft).
printf '%s' "$identity" | grep -Eq '^run/[0-9]+/job/[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$' || {
  echo "::error::RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY '$identity' does not match 'run/<id>/job/<name>' — the draft lifecycle guard could never reclaim such a draft" >&2
  exit 1
}

# Already created (by a sibling leg, the attach path, or a previous run)?
# Drafts and published releases both resolve here — upload-only is safe.
if gh release view "$tag" --repo "$repo" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "release $tag already exists — lazy draft create skipped"
  exit 0
fi

# Body: curated notes (CHANGELOG section / Unreleased / conventional
# commits) plus the ownership marker the guard verifies before deleting.
# stderr is NOT swallowed: release_notes.sh's ::error gates (e.g. the
# duplicate-'## Unreleased' curation guard) must stay visible even when
# the minimal fallback below keeps the train moving.
notes_file="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/release-lazy-notes.XXXXXX")"
trap 'rm -f "$notes_file"' EXIT
if ! bash "$(dirname "$0")/release_notes.sh" "$tag" >"$notes_file" ||
  [ ! -s "$notes_file" ]; then
  printf 'Release %s — see the CHANGELOG.\n' "$tag" >"$notes_file"
fi
# gh-237: bound the body BEFORE stamping the owner marker — the cap
# truncates from the TAIL, so a pre-stamped marker is cut off and the
# created draft carries no ownership proof: release_draft_guard.sh
# resolves `<unmarked>` and refuses to reclaim it, the daily sweeper
# buckets it human (the legs run with GH_TOKEN=RELEASE_PAT) and keeps
# it, dedupe ignores it — a forever-orphaned draft (gh-282). Bounded
# body (≤ 120,000) + the marker stays under the 125,000-character
# release-body cap whose overshoot HTTP-422'd `gh release create` in
# run 44680647719 (v1.0.756) and left every attach gate on the tag
# dying with "release not found".
bash "$(dirname "$0")/release_notes_cap.sh" "$notes_file"

marker="<!-- release-draft-owner: $identity -->"
grep -qF "$marker" "$notes_file" || printf '\n%s\n' "$marker" >>"$notes_file"

# gh-2026: a `gh release create` for a MISSING ref REST-mints a
# lightweight API tag with NO push event — the v0.1.408 silent class
# (issue #597). The fast legs (build-macos.yml build-extension /
# build-macos-cli) can reach this create before the attach legs
# (release-macos / release-mobile): the silent mint wins the race, every
# attach leg then finds the tag existing and skips the CI-firing
# annotated push, no tag train ever runs, and the draft is stranded
# (swept a day later — the v1.0.663 / v1.0.665 shape). When the ref is
# DEFINITELY missing, mint it through the CI-firing annotated push and
# verify the train started BEFORE creating the draft (dispatch-time call
# sites export GH_TOKEN=RELEASE_PAT for exactly this; the ci.yml tag-run
# call sites always see the tag of their own push event and never enter
# the mint). An indeterminable verdict (no origin remote, rc 128 —
# sandboxed fixtures) falls through to the plain create path.
set +e
git ls-remote --exit-code origin "refs/tags/$tag" >/dev/null 2>&1
ls_remote_rc=$?
set -e
if [ "$ls_remote_rc" -eq 2 ]; then
  bash "$(dirname "$0")/release_tag_mint.sh" "$tag"
fi

# DRAFT-first (gh-1801): a create here must never publish — the resolved
# asset list at this point can never include the signed checksums. The
# race-lost create is tolerated (the winner owns the release), but a REAL
# create failure is not (gh-237): the body was already bounded above by
# release_notes_cap.sh, so a surviving failure is a genuine API error.
create_rc=0
gh release create "$tag" \
  --repo "$repo" \
  --title "$tag" \
  --draft \
  --notes-file "$notes_file" || create_rc=$?
if [ "$create_rc" -eq 0 ]; then
  # gh-2372: the create SUCCEEDED, but a same-run sibling leg may have
  # created its own draft inside the view→create race window (GitHub
  # does not enforce one release per tag for drafts — the v1.0.760 /
  # v1.0.763 twin rot). The older (first-created) same-tag release must
  # win: self-delete OUR twin when we lost, so the caller attaches into
  # the winner and nothing rots for 24h until the sweeper. Best-effort.
  bash "$(dirname "$0")/release_draft_twin_dedupe.sh" "$tag"
  echo "✅ lazy draft ready for $tag (owner $identity) — publish is provenance-owned (gh-1801)"
  exit 0
fi
if [ "$create_rc" -ne 0 ]; then
  # gh-1801's `|| true` tolerated ONLY the view→create race — a sibling
  # leg creating the release between our view and create. gh-237 (run
  # 44680647719, v1.0.756): that swallow ALSO ate real create failures
  # (body-too-long 422), printed "✅ lazy draft ready", and failed every
  # attach gate with "release not found". Re-view: the release existing
  # NOW means we lost the race (upload into the winner's release); it
  # still being missing means the create itself failed — the leg must
  # go red, there is nothing to attach to.
  if gh release view "$tag" --repo "$repo" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "release create failed but $tag now exists — lost the view→create race, the winner owns the release"
    echo "✅ lazy draft ready for $tag (owner $identity) — publish is provenance-owned (gh-1801)"
    exit 0
  fi
  echo "::error::the draft create for $tag failed (rc $create_rc) and no concurrent release appeared — nothing to attach to; fix the create failure above (e.g. the release body exceeding the 125,000-character API cap, gh-237)" >&2
  exit 1
fi

Focus back on v1.0.78. Root cause of THIS ticket's finding: the three hosted "Build native binaries" legs died on `HTTP 500` from `gh release create` (POST /releases), each at the FIRST attempt, no retry. One of the creates evidently landed server-side anyway (the draft existed later), but the jobs' immediate re-view didn't see it (or it landed between the last re-view and the macOS jobs' reads).

Now — what's the right minimal fix in this repo? The repo has an established pattern for exactly this class of problem: transient GitHub API errors get retried. E.g.:
- gh-2072: sqlite3 native-assets prewarm retries 8 attempts per target ("a transient GitHub error page red'd four legs").
- gh-1724: test-core artifact uploads ride a retry ("retries stay always()-reachable and never continue-on-error").

Let me look for existing retry helpers in the repo scripts (e.g. a `with_retry` function in scripts/) to follow the established convention. Also let me check ci.yml's "Build native binaries" steps and see exactly what surrounds `release_lazy_draft.sh`, plus `release_asset_gate.sh` (the attach step — it may also benefit, but minimal fix = the create).

Also — IMPORTANT — the second error in the windows log: `scripts/release_draft_guard.sh: line 36: 1: usage: release_draft_guard.sh <tag>`. Let me read release_draft_guard.sh line 36 — the guard is invoked as `bash scripts/release_draft_guard.sh "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"` and failed with "1: usage". Wait, `GITHUB_REF_NAME` on windows-latest should be `v1.0.78`... The error format `line 36: 1: usage: release_draft_guard.sh <tag>` looks like bash's error for `${1:?usage: ...}` — i.e., the first positional was UNSET: "line 36: 1: usage: release_draft_guard.sh <tag>". Yes! `${1:?usage: release_lazy_draft.sh <tag>}` prints `line 36: 1: usage: ...`. Hmm wait, but the message says "usage: release_draft_guard.sh <tag>" — so release_draft_guard.sh has `${1:?usage: release_draft_guard.sh <tag>}` at line 36 and $1 was UNSET. That means `bash scripts/release_draft_guard.sh "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"` got an EMPTY GITHUB_REF_NAME.

But wait — in the ubuntu logs, the guard step said "release lifecycle guard: v1.0.78 is missing (published or absent) — nothing to clean" — GITHUB_REF_NAME was fine there. On Windows... the same env var should be set. Hmm, actually looking at the windows log again:

``
Build native binaries (windows-latest...)	... `bash scripts/release_draft_guard.sh "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"`
shell: C:\Program Files\PowerShell\7\pwsh.EXE -command ". '{0}'"
...
scripts/release_draft_guard.sh: line 36: 1: usage: release_draft_guard.sh <tag>
``

Hmm interesting — the step's `shell:` on windows is pwsh — `". '{0}'"` — the default `shell: bash` isn't used? Actually for the ubuntu job the guard step showed `shell: /usr/bin/bash -e {0}`. On windows it shows pwsh. That means the workflow's guard step has a default shell that differs... wait no, on GitHub Actions, `run:` steps on Windows default to pwsh UNLESS the workflow sets `defaults.run.shell: bash` at job/workflow level. The lazy-draft step on windows DID run with bash (`C:\Program Files\Git\bin\bash.EXE --noprofile --norc -e -o pipefail {0}`) — so THAT step specifies `shell: bash` explicitly. The guard step on windows ran under pwsh and... `${GITHUB_REF_NAME}` in pwsh? No wait — `run: bash scripts/release_draft_guard.sh "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"` under pwsh would expand `${GITHUB_REF_NAME}` how? In PowerShell, `${GITHUB_REF_NAME}` is a VARIABLE reference — in PowerShell syntax `${name}` IS valid variable syntax, but env vars in PowerShell are `$env:GITHUB_REF_NAME`, not `${GITHUB_REF_NAME}`. So under pwsh, `"${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"` evaluates to... PowerShell parses `${GITHUB_REF_NAME}` as a variable named GITHUB_REF_NAME which is undefined → empty string (with strict mode off, undefined variable → $null → empty in string interpolation). So the guard got called with NO argument → line 36 `${1:?usage:...}` error → guard exits 1 → step fails (it already failed from the lazy-draft step anyway; the job was already red).

So the windows job has a SECOND latent bug: the `release_draft_guard.sh` step runs under pwsh on Windows where `${GITHUB_REF_NAME}` expands to empty. In a SUCCESSFUL windows run, the lazy-draft step succeeds but then the guard step FAILS the whole job with the usage error! Wait — does it? `set -euo pipefail`... the guard is a separate `run:` step. If the guard exits non-zero, the step fails → job fails. Hmm, that would mean EVERY successful windows release leg would fail at the guard step... but v1.0.780/781 succeeded. Let me check how ci.yml invokes the guard for windows — maybe there's an `if:` or the step is configured `shell: bash`, and the pwsh shell shown in the FAILED log came from... hmm wait, the log clearly showed pwsh for the guard step on windows-latest. But v1.0.780 succeeded with the same workflow file... unless the workflow changed between 78 and 780.

The train run 45643151796 checked out tag v1.0.78 (commit 5fe937b). The current main may have different ci.yml. Let me diff ci.yml's binaries-matrix section at the v1.0.78 tag vs now, and see the guard step's shell. Actually, let me fetch the ci.yml at tag v1.0.78.

# gh-1280 NG2: «compiles» is not «works» — every release arch boots its
      # binary before the asset is archived/uploaded (same smoke as
      # binaries-pr). The usage marker (cli_help.dart "USAGE") discriminates
      # the real CLI help from a binary that merely prints something.
      - name: Smoke — the binary runs (fa --help)
        shell: bash
        run: |
          bin="build/out/bundle/bin/fa"
          [ "${{ matrix.os }}" = "windows" ] && bin="build/out/bundle/bin/fa.exe"
          out=$("$bin" --help)
          echo "$out"
          grep -qi "usage" <<<"$out" || { echo "fa --help did not print usage"; exit 1; }

      - name: Archive bundle
        shell: bash
        run: |
          archive_name="fa-${{ matrix.os }}-${{ matrix.arch }}"
          if [ "${{ matrix.archive }}" = "zip" ]; then
            asset="${archive_name}.zip"
            cd build/out && 7z a -tzip "../../$asset" bundle && cd -
          else
            asset="${archive_name}.tar.gz"
            tar -czf "$asset" -C build/out bundle
          fi
          ls -lh "$asset"

      - name: Upload archive to GitHub Release
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          # Matrix legs share GITHUB_JOB=binaries — the leg-suffixed draft
          # owner identity keeps the failure-path guard scoped to the leg
          # that created the draft, never a sibling's mid-upload one.
          RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY: run/${{ github.run_id }}/job/${{ github.job }}-${{ matrix.os }}-${{ matrix.arch }}
        run: |
          archive_name="fa-${{ matrix.os }}-${{ matrix.arch }}"
          if [ "${{ matrix.archive }}" = "zip" ]; then
            asset="${archive_name}.zip"
          else
            asset="${archive_name}.tar.gz"
          fi
          # gh-1801 (rework): DRAFT-first, publish is PROVENANCE-OWNED. The
          # CLI tarball is a `fa update` asset, but servability needs the
          # SIGNED SHA256SUMS — which only the release-provenance job can
          # upload (it needs the whole matrix + web-spa). So: create the
          # draft lazily (curated notes + a draft-owner marker the
          # lifecycle guard can reclaim), upload THIS leg's
          # fa-*.tar.gz/zip, and let release-provenance own the
          # --draft=false --latest flip after the checksums land.
          bash scripts/release_lazy_draft.sh "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"
          # gh-2042 AC1: the immutability gate owns the attach — a
          # PUBLISHED release skips already-attached assets, refuses
          # unattached fa-* assets loud, and re-signing goes through
          # release-provenance only.
          bash scripts/release_asset_gate.sh "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" "$asset"

      # Draft lifecycle invariant (issue #282 / gh-1801): this job creates
      # release drafts — a failed/cancelled leg must not leave its own
      # behind. Ownership-scoped (review of #294): deletes only a draft
      # stamped with THIS leg's RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY; a sibling leg's
      # mid-upload draft is never touched.
      - name: Draft lifecycle guard (delete orphaned draft on failure)
        if: always() && job.status != 'success'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY: run/${{ github.run_id }}/job/${{ github.job }}-${{ matrix.os }}-${{ matrix.arch }}
        run: bash scripts/release_draft_guard.sh "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"

  # Rehostable web SPA bundle (issue #1100): every release ships
  # fa-web-spa.zip — the release web build with <base href> rewritten to
  # ./, so it rehosts on any static host (incl. path-prefixed) or sandboxed
  # iframe with zero edits (docs/web-rehosting.md). Same build command AND
  # base-href as the Pages deploy; scripts/package_web_spa.sh patches the
  # tag on a COPY and enforces the absolute-path guard (AC3) before zipping.
  # Lives here, not in pages.yml: release commits (pubspec/CHANGELOG bumps)
  # fall outside pages.yml's path filters, so a Pages-produced bundle could
  # never attach to the actual release commit.
  web-spa:
    name: Build web SPA bundle
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

Found the SECOND bug! The "Draft lifecycle guard" step:

```yaml

       if: always() && job.status != 'success'

       run: bash scripts/release_draft_guard.sh "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"
``

**No `shell: bash`!** On windows-latest, `run:` defaults to pwsh → `"${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"` expands to EMPTY in PowerShell → guard gets no argument → `${1:?usage: release_draft_guard.sh <tag>}` fires → guard exits 1. With `if: always() && job.status != 'success'` the step only runs on failure, so on Windows failures this guard can NEVER do its job — it dies on the missing argument before deleting the orphaned draft!

Wait, also compare with the RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY used here: `run/.../job/binaries-windows-x64` — matches the log (RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY: run/45643151796/job/binaries-linux-x64). Hmm — the log shows `binaries-linux-x64` = `${ github.job }}-${ matrix.os }}-${ matrix.arch }}` where github.job="binaries". OK.

BUT WAIT. There's a mismatch with the sweper! The sweep script validates the marker shape `^run/[0-9]+/job/[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$` and parses `release-draft-owner: run/(?<run>[0-9]+)/job/`. Fine.

Now the guard failure on windows: the guard step ran `if: always() && job.status != 'success'` (the job failed) and under pwsh got an empty arg → died with usage error → did NOT delete the orphaned draft stamped `run/45643151796/job/binaries-windows-x64`. Same for the linux legs? On ubuntu the guard DID run with the right arg: "release lifecycle guard: v1.0.78 is missing (published or absent) — nothing to clean" — because the draft wasn't visible at that moment (the 500-create paradox: at 15:53:12.97 the re-view inside release_lazy_draft.sh said missing AND the guard said missing — consistent: the draft was not yet visible; it appeared later).

So the sequence makes sense now:
1. The three hosted legs each attempted `gh release create` → HTTP 500 → their re-view (0.5s later) → still missing → leg red.
2. The legs' failure-path guards (ubuntu legs: ran fine, found nothing — the draft wasn't visible yet; windows leg: died on the pwsh empty-arg bug — would have found nothing anyway at that moment).
3. ONE of the three 500'd creates actually landed server-side (draft created, response failed) — the draft materialized minutes later; macOS legs at 16:06/16:10 found it and attached.
4. release-provenance SKIPPED (needs the whole binaries matrix? — the matrix failed) → draft never published.
5. Daily sweper reclaimed it early + filed THIS issue (gh-2432), naming the failed train.

So there are two genuine product bugs to fix:

**Bug A (the root cause of the red train):** `release_lazy_draft.sh` performs a single-atempt `gh release create`. A transient GitHub API HTTP 500 (the create evidently landed server-side; response generation failed) reds three matrix legs simultaneously, skips release-provenance, kills the train, and strands the staged draft (reclaimed next sweep — recurring issue re-filed). The repo's established remedy for this exact class (transient GitHub error red'ing release legs — gh-2072, gh-1724) is retry-with-backoff. Fix: retry the create on failure with bounded attempts + short backoff, treating "release now exists" (race lost OR our earlier attempt landed server-side) as success at every retry boundary. Also treat the post-500 re-view more generously... but the minimal, convention-following fix: bounded retries with the existing race-tolerant checks inside the loop.

Wait — but careful: if the create actually landed server-side with an empty tag... hmm, no — the macOS legs found it via `gh release view v1.0.78`, so the tag was correct.

Also note: the re-view immediately after the 500 returned "missing" — replication lag. A retry loop naturally covers this: attempt 2 (5-10s later) would see the release exists → "lost the race / our landed create" → exit 0 → leg green → matrix green → provenance runs → publish. 

**Bug B (lifecycle guard broken exactly when needed on windows):** the failure-path "Draft lifecycle guard" step in ci.yml's binaries matrix lacks `shell: bash`, so on windows-latest it runs under pwsh, `"${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"` expands empty, the guard dies on `${1:?usage}` and never deletes the leg's orphaned draft. That's a real lifecycle-guard gap (the ticket's closing line: "recurrence means a lifecycle guard is missing") — the guard is missing ITS EFFECT precisely on the failed windows leg. Fix: add `shell: bash` to that step.

Both are in scope as "minimum targeted fix for the root cause". Bug A is the root cause of the failure; Bug B is the guard that should have cleaned up but couldn't (and the ticket's hint about a missing lifecycle guard).

# step below uploads it for fetch+commit; committed floor afterwards.
      - name: Size manifest + budget gate (fa-web-spa.zip)
        run: |
          python3 scripts/size_manifest.py check fa-web-spa.zip \
            --baseline scripts/size_budget/web-spa.tsv --init-if-missing

      - name: Upload seeded size baselines (#1096 ratchet)
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: size-baselines-web-spa
          path: scripts/size_budget/*.tsv
          if-no-files-found: ignore

      - name: Upload bundle to GitHub Release
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          # gh-1801 (rework): DRAFT-first and NEVER publish here. The web
          # zip is not a `fa update` asset — and even a CLI asset alone
          # would not make the release servable: the SIGNED SHA256SUMS
          # only lands in release-provenance, which owns the
          # --draft=false --latest flip. Create/attach the draft with the
          # curated notes + a draft-owner marker (guard/sweeper-visible)
          # and upload.
          # No guard step here ON PURPOSE: this job is continue-on-error —
          # on failure the train (binaries → provenance) CONTINUES and
          # must find the draft alive; a genuinely orphaned draft is
          # reclaimed by the 24h sweeper (GITHUB_TOKEN-authored → bot).
          bash scripts/release_lazy_draft.sh "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"
          # gh-2042 AC1: the immutability gate owns the attach (published
          # releases are immutable for fa-* assets — skip/refuse, never clobber).
          bash scripts/release_asset_gate.sh "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" fa-web-spa.zip

      # continue-on-error keeps the job/check green even on failure — a
      # release can then only be gated on a MISSING asset. Surface the miss
      # in the run's step summary too (covers upload flakes, not just guard
      # trips); the failed steps remain visible in the job view.
      - name: Flag missing bundle in step summary
        if: failure()
        run: |
          {
            echo '## fa-web-spa.zip NOT shipped this release'
            echo ''

content.text: IDENTICAL between v1.0.778 and main

# The details reset runs BEFORE any download (gh-2042 review): a check that
# dies mid-download must never leave stale checkout content behind for the
# remediation step to page as if it were today's drift.
rm -f "$details"

workdir="${FA_DRIFT_LOCAL_DIR:-$(mktemp -d)}"

# Download with a transient-blip guard (gh-2042 review): retry once on
# transport failures (502, rate limit, ...) and treat ONLY an explicit
# not-found / no-match verdict as a deterministic "absent" (rc 2). Any
# other failure after the retry is infra (rc 1).
gh_dl() { # gh_dl <pattern> → 0 downloaded, 2 deterministic absent, 1 infra
  local pattern="$1" attempt err rc
  for attempt in 1 2; do
    err=$(mktemp)
    rc=0
    gh release download "$tag" --repo "$repo" --dir "$workdir" --pattern "$pattern" 2>"$err" || rc=$?
    if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then
      rm -f "$err"
      return 0
    fi
    if grep -Eqi 'not found|no assets match' "$err"; then
      rm -f "$err"
      return 2
    fi
    rm -f "$err"
    if [ "$attempt" -lt 2 ]; then
      sleep "${FA_DRIFT_RETRY_SLEEP:-2}"
    fi
  done
  return 1
}

if [ -z "${FA_DRIFT_LOCAL_DIR:-}" ]; then
  mkdir -p "$workdir"
  # The manifest and its signature ride their own pattern: `fa-*` does not
  # match them, and BOTH must be on the release for provenance to exist.
  fa_rc=0
  sha_rc=0
  gh_dl 'fa-*' || fa_rc=$?
  gh_dl 'SHA256SUMS*' || sha_rc=$?
  if [ "$fa_rc" -eq 1 ] || [ "$sha_rc" -eq 1 ]; then
    echo "::error::release drift check could not download the assets of $tag (transport error after retry) — an infra blip is NOT drift evidence: failing WITHOUT a drift page; the next scheduled run re-checks" >&2
    exit 2
  fi

import re, glob
# Scan every workflow: for jobs whose runs-on can be windows, find run: steps invoking `bash scripts/...` without an explicit shell: bash
for f in sorted(glob.glob(".github/workflows/*.yml")):
    text = open(f).read()
    lines = text.splitlines()
    # find jobs: top-level "  <name>:"
    job_starts = [(i, m.group(1)) for i, l in enumerate(lines) if (m := re.match(r"^  ([A-Za-z0-9_-]+):\s*$", l))]
    job_starts.append((len(lines), None))
    for k in range(len(job_starts)-1):
        start, job = job_starts[k]; end = job_starts[k+1][0]
        body = "\n".join(lines[start:end])
        if "runs-on:" not in body: continue
        runs_on = re.findall(r"runs-on:\s*(.+)", body)
        windows = any("windows" in r for r in runs_on)
        if not windows: continue
        # find run: steps invoking bash scripts
        step_iter = list(re.finditer(r"(?:^|\n)(\s*)- (?:name:.*\n(?:.*\n)*?)?(\s*)(?:shell:\s*(\S+)(?:.*\n)?)?(\s*)run:\s*[|>]?\s*\n?((?:\1\s{4,}.*\n?)*)", body))
        # simpler: iterate lines, track last - name:, shell: and run: block
        cur_name, cur_shell = None, None
        run_block = []
        j = start
        while j < end:
            l = lines[j]
            if re.match(r"\s*- name:", l):
                # evaluate previous step
                if run_block:
                    joined = "\n".join(run_block)
                    if "bash scripts/" in joined and cur_shell != "bash":
                        print(f"{f} job={job} step={cur_name!r} shell={cur_shell} line≈{j+1}")
                cur_name = l.strip(); cur_shell = None; run_block = []
            elif re.match(r"\s*shell:", l):
                cur_shell = l.split(":")[1].strip()
            elif re.match(r"\s*run:", l) or (run_block and l.strip() and not re.match(r"\s*- |if:|uses:|env:|with:|shell:", l) and cur_name):
                run_block.append(l)
            j += 1
        if run_block:
            joined = "\n".join(run_block)
            if "bash scripts/" in joined and cur_shell != "bash":
                print(f"{f} job={job} step={cur_name!r} shell={cur_shell} (last)")

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Release draft lifecycle guard (issue #282): a run that creates a release
# draft must end with it published or deleted — never orphan it. `gh
# release create <tag> <assets...>` uploads the assets through a DRAFT
# first and publishes only after every upload succeeds; a step dying
# mid-upload (the v0.1.190 rot) leaves that draft behind forever.
#
# Usage: release_draft_guard.sh <tag>
#
# OWNERSHIP-SCOPED DELETE (review of #294): the guard deletes ONLY the
# draft this very run+job created. daily-publish runs the macOS and
# mobile legs concurrently against the same derived tag; a failed leg's
# guard firing on the SIBLING leg's mid-upload draft would destroy a
# healthy concurrent release. Draft-capable creates
# (scripts/release_attach_or_create.sh, scripts/release_lazy_draft.sh)
# stamp the draft body with
#   <!-- release-draft-owner: run/<run_id>/job/<job_id> -->
# and the guard deletes only on an exact match against GITHUB_RUN_ID /
# GITHUB_JOB (both GitHub Actions default env). Matrix jobs share
# GITHUB_JOB across legs (ci.yml binaries, build-macos.yml
# build-macos-cli) — those steps stamp a LEG-SUFFIXED identity via
# RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY (e.g. run/123/job/binaries-linux-x64) and the
# guard step must export the same value, so a failed leg can never match
# a sibling's in-flight draft. A foreign or unmarked draft is NEVER
# deleted here — the daily sweeper
# (scripts/sweep_stale_drafts.sh) reclaims genuinely orphaned drafts
# after 24h.
#
# Called from workflow steps with `if: always() && job.status != 'success'`
# so it runs on failure AND cancellation. A published release or a missing
# release is a no-op; a draft for <tag> is deleted (its assets are
# unpublished by definition — published releases are the artifact store,
# issue #282 E2). The tag itself is never touched.
set -euo pipefail

tag="${1:?usage: release_draft_guard.sh <tag>}"
repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:?GITHUB_REPOSITORY must be set}"
: "${GITHUB_RUN_ID:?GITHUB_RUN_ID must be set (GitHub Actions default env)}"
: "${GITHUB_JOB:?GITHUB_JOB must be set (GitHub Actions default env)}"

arguments.content:
# Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: The v1.0.778 release train died on three transient GitHub-API `HTTP 500`s during the release-draft create, release-provenance (the sole publish point) was skipped, and the staged draft rotted until the daily sweeper reclaimed it early — re-filing the recurring sweep issue (gh-2432). The failure-path lifecycle guard that should have cleaned the windows leg's draft could not even run there.

**Root cause** (two defects, both confirmed from the failing run's logs, run 45643151796):

1. `scripts/release_lazy_draft.sh` (create path) attempts `gh release create` **exactly once**. At 15:53–15:54 all three hosted binaries legs (linux-x64, linux-arm64, windows-x64) got `HTTP 500 (…/repos/…/releases)` from the create (each body was already bounded to 119,961 bytes by `release_notes_cap.sh` — this was NOT the gh-237 422 body-cap). The single post-failure `gh release view` re-check (~0.5 s later) still saw nothing, so each leg went red. The draft **did** materialize minutes later (the self-hosted macOS legs' `release_lazy_draft.sh` printed "release v1.0.778 already exists — lazy draft create skipped" at 16:06:34/16:10:33), i.e. at least one 500'd attempt landed server-side but nothing in-run ever re-checked. Three red matrix legs → `Sign release checksums` (release-provenance, the sole publish point) skipped → the staged draft's publish point unreachable → the daily sweeper reclaimed it early (gh-2318 criterion) and counted the reclaim as a sweep finding → this issue. A transient server 5xx red's an entire release train; the repo already treats transient GitHub errors on release legs as retry-class (release_drift_check.sh `gh_dl` retry, gh-2072 sqlite3 prewarm, gh-1724 upload retry).
2. `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `binaries` job, step "Draft lifecycle guard (delete orphaned draft on failure)" — the step has **no `shell: bash`**. It is the only `bash scripts/…`-invoking `run:` step in a windows-capable matrix job repo-wide without one. On the windows-latest row the default shell is pwsh, where `"${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"` interpolates an *undefined PowerShell variable* → empty → the guard died on `${1:?usage: release_draft_guard.sh <tag>}` (`scripts/release_draft_guard.sh: line 36: 1: usage: …` in the job log). The issue-#282 failure-path cleanup therefore **never runs on the windows leg** — precisely the "lifecycle guard is missing" the ticket warns about. (Linux/macOS rows default to bash, masking the bug.)

**Impact**: Any transient GitHub API 5xx on the create simultaneously reds every hosted binaries leg, skips release-provenance, and kills the whole train (v1.0.778 never shipped; `Advance vpinned marker` fail-closed, no SHA256SUMS). The staged draft is stranded for the sweeper to reclaim and the sweep issue re-files — the recurring pattern this ticket documents. Independently, on any windows-leg failure the orphan-draft guard is a no-op (usage error), so a leg-owned draft can rot until the 24h sweeper.

**Fix approach**:
- `scripts/release_lazy_draft.sh`: retry the create with a small bounded loop on **transient** server errors only (HTTP 500/502/503/504 / "server error"), keeping the existing race re-view at every retry boundary — which also heals the exact v1.0.778 shape ("500 landed server-side", one create attempt, leg green). Deterministic 4xx (gh-237 422 body-too-long) still fails loud after exactly one attempt. Knobs follow the repo convention: `RELEASE_LAZY_CREATE_TRIES` (default 3), `RELEASE_LAZY_CREATE_SLEEP` (default 2).
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: add `shell: bash` to the binaries "Draft lifecycle guard" step so it runs the same on every matrix row.

**Previous attempt**: none — this is the first fix leg for gh-2432 (twelve earlier dev runs produced no commits on `ai/gh-2432`).

# race-lost create is tolerated (the winner owns the release), but a REAL
# create failure is not (gh-237): the body was already bounded above by
# release_notes_cap.sh, so a surviving failure is a genuine API error.
#
# gh-2432 (run 45643151796, v1.0.778): that single shot made every
# TRANSIENT GitHub API server error fatal. All three hosted binaries legs
# got `HTTP 500 (…/releases)` from the create within two minutes (the body
# was already bounded to 119,961 bytes — NOT the gh-237 422 cap), each
# leg's lone post-failure re-view ~0.5s later still saw nothing, and the
# train red'd: release-provenance (the sole publish point) was skipped and
# the staged draft rotted until the daily sweeper reclaimed it (the
# recurring sweep issue gh-2432). One 500'd attempt evidently CREATED the
# draft server-side — the self-hosted macOS legs resolved it minutes
# later — but nothing in-run ever re-checked. Retry TRANSIENT 5xx only,
# with the race re-view at every failure boundary (which heals the
# landed-500 shape with a single create); a deterministic 4xx cannot
# answer differently on attempt 2 and still fails loud after exactly one
# attempt (gh-237 contract). Knobs follow the repo's env-override
# convention (RELEASE_TRAIN_VERIFY_TRIES/SLEEP, FA_DRIFT_RETRY_SLEEP):
# RELEASE_LAZY_CREATE_TRIES (default 3) / RELEASE_LAZY_CREATE_SLEEP
# (default 2s).
create_rc=0
create_tries="${RELEASE_LAZY_CREATE_TRIES:-3}"
create_sleep="${RELEASE_LAZY_CREATE_SLEEP:-2}"
create_err="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/release-lazy-create.XXXXXX")"
trap 'rm -f "$notes_file" "$create_err"' EXIT
attempt=1
while :; do
  create_rc=0
  gh release create "$tag" \
    --repo "$repo" \
    --title "$tag" \
    --draft \
    --notes-file "$notes_file" 2>"$create_err" || create_rc=$?
  # gh's stderr must stay in the Actions log ("fix the create failure
  # above", gh-237) — the capture file is a CLASSIFIER, not a sink.
  [ -s "$create_err" ] && cat "$create_err" >&2
  if [ "$create_rc" -eq 0 ]; then
    break
  fi
  # gh-1801's `|| true` tolerated ONLY the view→create race — a sibling
  # leg creating the release between our view and create. gh-237 (run
  # 44680647719, v1.0.756): that swallow ALSO ate real create failures
  # (body-too-long 422), printed "✅ lazy draft ready", and failed every
  # attach gate with "release not found". Re-view at EVERY failure
  # boundary now: the release existing means we lost the race — or our
  # own 500'd-but-landed attempt materialized late (the v1.0.778 shape);
  # either way the caller uploads into the winner's release.
  if gh release view "$tag" --repo "$repo" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "release create failed but $tag now exists — lost the view→create race, the winner owns the release"
    echo "✅ lazy draft ready for $tag (owner $identity) — publish is provenance-owned (gh-1801)"
    exit 0
  fi
  if [ "$attempt" -lt "$create_tries" ] \
    && grep -Eq 'HTTP 5[0-9][0-9]' "$create_err" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "transient GitHub API error on the draft create (attempt $attempt of $create_tries) — retrying in ${create_sleep}s" >&2
    attempt=$((attempt + 1))
    sleep "$create_sleep"
    continue
  fi
  break
done
if [ "$create_rc" -eq 0 ]; then
  # gh-2372: the create SUCCEEDED, but a same-run sibling leg may have
  # created its own draft inside the view→create race window (GitHub
  # does not enforce one release per tag for drafts — the v1.0.760 /
  # v1.0.763 twin rot). The older (first-created) same-tag release must
  # win: self-delete OUR twin when we lost, so the caller attaches into
  # the winner and nothing rots for 24h until the sweeper. Best-effort.
  bash "$(dirname "$0")/release_draft_twin_dedupe.sh" "$tag"
  echo "✅ lazy draft ready for $tag (owner $identity) — publish is provenance-owned (gh-1801)"
  exit 0
fi
echo "::error::the draft create for $tag failed (rc $create_rc) and no concurrent release appeared — nothing to attach to; fix the create failure above (e.g. the release body exceeding the 125,000-character API cap, gh-237)" >&2
exit 1

Run 45643151796 (v1.0.778): all three hosted binaries legs got
'HTTP 500 (.../releases)' from the single-shot 'gh release create'
(body already bounded to 119,961 bytes — not the gh-237 422 cap), no
in-run retry re-checked, the train red'd, release-provenance (the sole
publish point) was skipped and the staged draft rotted until the daily
sweeper reclaimed it (recurring sweep issue gh-2432). One 500'd attempt
evidently landed server-side — the macOS legs resolved the draft minutes
later — but nothing ever looked again.

- release_lazy_draft.sh: bounded retry on TRANSIENT HTTP 5xx only
  (RELEASE_LAZY_CREATE_TRIES/SLEEP, default 3 x 2s, gh_dl convention),
  race re-view at every failure boundary (heals the landed-500 shape
  with a single create); a deterministic 4xx still fails loud after
  exactly one attempt (gh-237 contract pinned by test).
- ci.yml binaries 'Draft lifecycle guard': pin 'shell: bash' — the only
  bash-scripts run-step in a windows-capable matrix job without one; on
  windows-latest the pwsh default interpolated \"\${GITHUB_REF_NAME}\"
  as an undefined PowerShell variable (empty) and the guard died on
  '\${1:?usage}' (job log: 'line 36: 1: usage: release_draft_guard.sh
  <tag>') — the issue-#282 orphan-draft cleanup never ran there.

Tests: 4 new gh-2432 behavioral cases in release_lazy_draft_mint_test.dart
(retry-heals, landed-500 heals via the re-view, bounded tries exhaust
loud, 422 never retried) + repo-wide static guard

content.text:
# Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: The v1.0.778 release train died on three transient GitHub-API `HTTP 500`s during the release-draft create, release-provenance (the sole publish point) was skipped, and the staged draft rotted until the daily sweeper reclaimed it early — re-filing the recurring sweep issue (gh-2432). The failure-path lifecycle guard that should have cleaned the windows leg's draft could not even run there.

**Root cause** (two defects, both confirmed from the failing run's logs, run 45643151796):

1. `scripts/release_lazy_draft.sh` (create path) attempts `gh release create` **exactly once**. At 15:53–15:54 all three hosted binaries legs (linux-x64, linux-arm64, windows-x64) got `HTTP 500 (…/repos/…/releases)` from the create (each body was already bounded to 119,961 bytes by `release_notes_cap.sh` — this was NOT the gh-237 422 body-cap). The single post-failure `gh release view` re-check (~0.5 s later) still saw nothing, so each leg went red. The draft **did** materialize minutes later (the self-hosted macOS legs' `release_lazy_draft.sh` printed "release v1.0.778 already exists — lazy draft create skipped" at 16:06:34/16:10:33), i.e. at least one 500'd attempt landed server-side but nothing in-run ever re-checked. Three red matrix legs → `Sign release checksums` (release-provenance, the sole publish point) skipped → the staged draft's publish point unreachable → the daily sweeper reclaimed it early (gh-2318 criterion) and counted the reclaim as a sweep finding → this issue. A transient server 5xx red's an entire release train; the repo already treats transient GitHub errors on release legs as retry-class (release_drift_check.sh `gh_dl` retry, gh-2072 sqlite3 prewarm, gh-1724 upload retry).
2. `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `binaries` job, step "Draft lifecycle guard (delete orphaned draft on failure)" — the step has **no `shell: bash`**. It is the only `bash scripts/…`-invoking `run:` step in a windows-capable matrix job repo-wide without one. On the windows-latest row the default shell is pwsh, where `"${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"` interpolates an *undefined PowerShell variable* → empty → the guard died on `${1:?usage: release_draft_guard.sh <tag>}` (`scripts/release_draft_guard.sh: line 36: 1: usage: …` in the job log). The issue-#282 failure-path cleanup therefore **never runs on the windows leg** — precisely the "lifecycle guard is missing" the ticket warns about. (Linux/macOS rows default to bash, masking the bug.)

**Impact**: Any transient GitHub API 5xx on the create simultaneously reds every hosted binaries leg, skips release-provenance, and kills the whole train (v1.0.778 never shipped; `Advance vpinned marker` fail-closed, no SHA256SUMS). The staged draft is stranded for the sweeper to reclaim and the sweep issue re-files — the recurring pattern this ticket documents. Independently, on any windows-leg failure the orphan-draft guard is a no-op (usage error), so a leg-owned draft can rot until the 24h sweeper.

**Fix approach**:
- `scripts/release_lazy_draft.sh`: retry the create with a small bounded loop on **transient** server errors only (HTTP 500/502/503/504 / "server error"), keeping the existing race re-view at every retry boundary — which also heals the exact v1.0.778 shape ("500 landed server-side", one create attempt, leg green). Deterministic 4xx (gh-237 422 body-too-long) still fails loud after exactly one attempt. Knobs follow the repo convention: `RELEASE_LAZY_CREATE_TRIES` (default 3), `RELEASE_LAZY_CREATE_SLEEP` (default 2).
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: add `shell: bash` to the binaries "Draft lifecycle guard" step so it runs the same on every matrix row.

**Previous attempt**: none — this is the first fix leg for gh-2432 (twelve earlier dev runs produced no commits on `ai/gh-2432`).

### Root Cause

Run 45643151796 (v1.0.778): all three hosted `binaries` legs got `HTTP 500 (…/releases)` from the **single-shot** `gh release create` in `scripts/release_lazy_draft.sh` (bodies were already bounded — not the gh-237 422), no in-run retry re-checked, and one 500'd attempt evidently landed server-side (the draft resolved minutes later to the macOS legs). Three red legs skipped release-provenance (the sole publish point), so the staged draft was unreachable and the daily sweeper reclaimed it — re-filing the recurring sweep issue. Separately, the failure-path "Draft lifecycle guard" step in ci.yml's `binaries` job had no `shell: bash`: on the windows-latest row pwsh interpolated `"${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"` as an undefined PowerShell variable (empty) and the guard died on `${1:?usage}` — the issue-#282 orphan-draft cleanup never runs on Windows.

### Fix

- `scripts/release_lazy_draft.sh`: bounded retry of the draft create on **transient HTTP 5xx only** (`RELEASE_LAZY_CREATE_TRIES`/`RELEASE_LAZY_CREATE_SLEEP`, default 3 × 2s, same convention as `gh_dl`/gh-2072), with the existing race re-view at every failure boundary — which heals the "500 landed server-side" shape after a single create. Deterministic 4xx still fails loud after exactly one attempt (gh-237 contract).
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: pin `shell: bash` on the `binaries` "Draft lifecycle guard" step.

### Test Coverage

- `test/release_lazy_draft_mint_test.dart` — 4 new gh-2432 cases: transient 500 retried → green; landed-500 healed via the re-view with exactly 1 create; 500 on every attempt fails loud after the bounded tries; 422 never retried. All passed.
- `test/ci_2432_draft_lifecycle_guard_shell_test.dart` — new repo-wide static guard (ci_2408 pattern): every `bash scripts/…` run-step in a windows-capable job pins an effective `shell: bash`; direct regression pin on the guard step + negative probes. All passed.
- Full unit suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` — 15,314 passed, 16 skipped, 0 failures.

### Notes

- No breaking changes: the retry keys on `HTTP 5xx` responses only; gh-237's single-attempt 422 failure and gh-1801/gh-2372 race/twin semantics are unchanged and pinned by their existing tests.
- v1.0.778 itself stays unreclaimed-by-train (superseded trains are never rerun; v1.0.779–.781 shipped after) — this PR prevents recurrence, per the ticket's "recurrence means a lifecycle guard is missing".

Three red legs → release-provenance (sole publish point) skipped → staged draft unreachable → sweeper reclaimed it early and re-filed this recurring issue.
2. **The "missing lifecycle guard" the ticket names** — ci.yml's `binaries` "Draft lifecycle guard" step had no `shell: bash`; on windows-latest the pwsh default interpolated `"${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"` as an *undefined PowerShell variable* (empty), so the guard died on `${1:?usage}` (`line 36: 1: usage: …` in the job log) and the issue-#282 orphan-draft cleanup never runs on Windows.
